istruzioni:
Archivist is shared, keyword-based memory for the coding agents on this team. Refining content is YOUR job — the server only stores and searches, it runs no LLM. Follow this protocol.

PROJECT NAMESPACE (uniqueness rule). Every tool takes a `project` slug; memory is shared by the whole team under it. Derive the slug from the git remote: take the repository name and normalize it — lowercase, drop the `.git` suffix, slugify. `git@github.com:acme/Billing-API.git` → `billing-api`. No remote → normalize the root directory name. NEVER invent or abbreviate the slug: teammates who pick different names split the namespace and never see each other's memory.

WRITE (save a concept).
1. Extract 1-3 keywords from the concept.
2. Keyword you know exists → refine a dense fragment ≤500 tokens and `memory_append` it. Never blocks, never conflicts.
3. New concept → write a mini-context (2000 soft / 10000 hard; over soft: `soft_cap_exceeded`, re-refine smaller) and `memory_upsert` it (omit `expected_version`). If the response lists `near_duplicates` and one is the same concept, self-correct now: `memory_delete` your new entry and `memory_append` a fragment to the existing keyword. Unsure whether a keyword exists? Probe first with `memory_search` `intent="write"`.
4. `compaction_due=true` → see COMPACTION.

RETRIEVE. Search BEFORE any non-trivial task and whenever you meet an unknown entity (module, tool, error, convention). `memory_search` with `intent="read"`, follow `related_keywords`; `memory_get` only the keywords that matter; `memory_list` to orient in a new project. Nothing found and the concept is cross-cutting → retry with `scope="all"`. Writes always stay in the current project. Results carry `age_days` — treat old entries with care, and if a memory contradicts what you observe in the code, fix it in the same turn with a correction fragment (`memory_append`).

COMPACTION (routine upkeep). When any response shows `compaction_due=true`, compact in the same turn if you can — no user permission needed; it is safe, every version is kept in history. Steps: `memory_get` the keyword, merge base + fragments into refined content (cap as WRITE), `memory_upsert` with the `expected_version` and `last_fragment_id` you read. `VERSION_CONFLICT` → someone compacted first: re-read, retry. Mid-task and cannot stop? Deferring is safe — every version is kept and the append queue is bounded — and if the team has the archivist-companion plugin, its `/archivist-companion:sweep` command reconciles overdue compactions; still, compact in-turn when you can.

CONTENT STYLE. Dense, factual, English, no fluff. Self-contained: readable months later without this session's context.

DO NOT SAVE. Secrets or credentials; framework/library trivia; anything recoverable from the code in ~10 seconds.

strumenti.description: Search shared memory by exact/prefix keyword and full text over content AND pending fragments. Returns ranked results (keyword, excerpt, score, pending_fragments, token_count, age_days) plus related_keywords to reuse instead of creating duplicates. scope='project' (default) searches the current project; scope='all' searches every project (each result carries its own project). Search BEFORE starting non-trivial work or when you hit an unknown entity. Pass intent='read' for a genuine retrieval or intent='write' for the pre-create dedup probe — an audit signal only, it does not affect results.
strumenti.name: memory_search

strumenti.description: Read entries by keyword: base content + pending fragments + version + last_fragment_id + compaction_due + token_total + age_days + fragment_count. Unknown keywords come back in not_found. If compaction_due is true, COMPACT NOW: merge the base and all fragments into one refined content and call memory_upsert with the returned expected_version and last_fragment_id. keywords takes a list, e.g. keywords=["design-system"]; a single keyword may also be passed as a bare string, e.g. keywords="design-system", and the singular keyword= is accepted as an alias.
strumenti.name: memory_get

strumenti.description: Append a refined fragment to an EXISTING entry — the default write path once a keyword exists. Never blocks, never conflicts. When the response has compaction_due=true the entry crossed the threshold: read it with memory_get and compact it via memory_upsert. If the keyword does not exist yet, create it with memory_upsert instead. The fragment goes in fragment= (content=, the name memory_upsert uses, is accepted as an alias).
strumenti.name: memory_append

strumenti.description: Create a new entry, or write a compaction result. New keyword: omit expected_version and pass the refined content — the entry is created at version 1. Existing keyword: this is a compaction — pass expected_version (from your memory_get read) to replace the base content and bump the version, and pass last_fragment_id to consume the fragments you merged (required whenever fragments are pending). A version mismatch returns VERSION_CONFLICT: re-read, merge again, retry. On create, the response may include near_duplicates (existing keywords that look like the same concept): if one matches, self-correct — memory_delete your new entry and memory_append a fragment to the existing keyword. Content has a 2000-token soft cap and a 10000-token hard cap: over 2000 the write still succeeds but returns soft_cap_exceeded + a warning — re-refine ~10% smaller and upsert again while it keeps compressing without losing data; over 10000 it is rejected.
strumenti.name: memory_upsert

strumenti.description: List every keyword in a project with token_count, pending_fragments, compaction_due and updated_at — use it to get oriented in a project.
strumenti.name: memory_list

strumenti.description: Soft-delete an entry (history is preserved). Returns deleted=true, or NOT_FOUND if the keyword is not present in the project.
strumenti.name: memory_delete

strumenti.description: Read the recorded version history of an entry (newest first): the content as it stood at each version, who wrote it, and when. Use it after a compaction to check what the merge dropped, or to recover wording that was compressed away. Read-only — it never changes state. Pass include_deleted=true to read the history of a PRUNED entry — that is how you check, or recover, what a forgetting sweep dropped.
strumenti.name: memory_history
